attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a NAT gateway for a new private network (10.10.20.0/24) shared with node2 and node3, using an Ansible playbook run from the control node (node4). node1's eth1 got address 10.10.20.1/24 plus a masquerade source-NAT rule out eth0; node2/node3 got static addresses (10.10.20.2/3) on enp8s0 via netplan and a preferred default route via node1. Verified processes on node2/node3 reach the internet (curl 1.1.1.1 -> HTTP 301) exclusively through node1's NAT (ip route get shows the private gateway as the path, and node1's nftables/conntrack show translated hits). All four nodes were then restarted one at a time via systemctl reboot, with boot_id changes proving real restarts and post-restart re-verification (NAT rule/interface persisted via VyOS saved config, netplan persisted on Ubuntu, Ansible re-run idempotent with continued internet reachability) confirming full recovery.
